title: Protecting Your Identity
drDigitalIntro:
Identity theft is when a thief uses your details to pretend to be you. They might open a bank account, buy things, or get into your email — all in your name.
• Never type your ID number, passport number, or bank details into a website unless you went there yourself and you are sure it is the real one.
• Guard your email and your bank the hardest. A thief who gets into your email can reset the password on everything else.
• Read your bank statement once a month. A small charge you do not recognize is often the first sign, long before anything big happens.
• Websites can follow you from site to site. Your computer has a setting to stop that. It is called Cross-Site Tracking, and turning it off is safe.
• If it does happen: call your bank first, then change your passwords, then report it. Acting the same day is what keeps the damage small.

playgroundTask.goal: Tighten your privacy settings to reduce tracking

steps.say: Click Privacy in the Settings sidebar.
Turn off Cross-Site Tracking — this stops websites following you across the web.
Turn off Location Sharing so websites cannot see where you are.

drDigitalSuccess: Your privacy settings are tighter! Turning off tracking makes it harder for data collectors to build a profile about you.
drDigitalHint: Open Privacy in the Settings sidebar, then click the toggles to turn off Cross-Site Tracking and Location Sharing.
